title: Epic breakdown
description: How the maintainer splits an epic into independently shippable issues. A script creates one issue per piece from this file, so it is the whole of what each issue says.

understanding.description: How you read the epic, and the clubbing test's answer for every adjacent pair of pieces. Posted on the epic with the list of issues.

why.description: What a user can do once this lands that they could not before.

context.description: What the planner of this piece needs from the epic that the acceptance lines do not say: the screens, the data, the constraints. Copied into the issue body as written.

covers.description: The TR- ids (and S- sections) this piece delivers. Written on the issue as its Covers: line; the epic does not close until everything its pieces cover was built by a completed piece or deferred.

depends_on.description: 1-based indexes of other pieces that must land first.

risk.description: Named when the piece touches money, auth, migrations or infra.

issue.description: Re-split only: the existing issue this piece is. Its title and body are rewritten from the piece. Ignored on a first split.

absorbs.description: Re-split only: existing issues folded into this piece. Give this piece their acceptance lines; each is closed with a comment naming this piece's issue.

what.description: The part of the epic not split out yet.

covers.description: The TR- ids (and S- sections) left to this deferral, so the epic can close without them honestly.

deferred.description: Parts of the epic deliberately not split out yet. Each is filed as its own issue labelled sdlc:deferred, so it is tracked rather than forgotten.

depends_on.description: The open epic it cannot be built before.

epic_links.description: Epics whose product genuinely cannot be built before another's. A script adds `Depends on #<depends_on>` to each `epic`; both must be open issues labelled sdlc:epic.

created.description: Ignored. The pipeline creates the issues from pieces[] and records their numbers itself.
